title: Ascorbate-nitrite reaction: possible means of blocking the formation of carcinogenic N-nitroso compounds
authors: Mirvish SS, Wallcave L, Eagen M, Shubik P
funder: Not read: the Science full text returned HTTP 403, the archived article page shows the abstract and reference list only, and Unpaywall lists no open copy. Affiliation of all authors: Eppley Institute for Research in Cancer, University of Nebraska Medical Center, Omaha.
result: Read in the abstract. Ascorbic acid blocked the formation of carcinogenic N-nitroso compounds by the chemical reaction between nitrous acid and oxytetracycline, morpholine, piperazine, N-methylaniline, methylurea and, in some experiments, dimethylamine; the extent of blocking depended on the compound nitrosated and on the experimental conditions. Urea and ammonium sulfamate were less effective blocking agents.
